Stay Senyati Safari Camp
stay your way
From camping under the stars to settling into a chalet or the unique Chobe Glamper, there’s more than one way to experience Senyati. Choose the accommodation that suits you and enjoy the freedom of having the bush right on your doorstep.
CHOBE GLAMPER
YOUR private retreat in the wild
Experience the freedom of sleeping close to nature with the comforts of a beautifully appointed private space. The Chobe Glamper features a plush bed, private bathroom, outdoor deck and braai area, giving you a unique way to experience the bush in comfort and privacy.
AMENITIES
Plush bed with quality linen
Electric blanket
Private bathroom
Hot-water bath and shower
Flushing toilet
Private patio
Private braai area
Fireplace
Nespresso coffee maker
Fridge
Bedside lighting
International power sockets
Electricity
Wi-Fi
Chalets
YOUR Home in the bush
Our self-catering chalets give you a comfortable place to settle in and make yourself at home. With your own kitchenette and braai area, you have the freedom to enjoy Senyati at your own pace, with the waterhole and lookout deck just a short walk away.
With different chalet configurations available, there’s space for couples, families and groups travelling together.

CAMPSITES
Your own space in the bush
Bring your tent, rooftop tent or caravan and enjoy the freedom of having your own space in the bush. Senyati’s spacious campsites offer private ablutions, hot water, electricity and your own braai area, giving you everything you need to camp comfortably and enjoy the outdoors.

About Senyati Safari Camp
ABOUT SENYATI
WHERE WILDLIFE COMES TO YOU
Set in the Lesoma Valley near Kasane, Botswana, Senyati Safari Camp has grown from a piece of bush into a place with its own character. Shaped by Louw and Lulu Barnard, the camp has always been about staying close to nature, experiencing wildlife up close and feeling at home in the bush.
from the bush to senyati
In 2008, Louw Barnard began developing the land that would become Senyati. Together with Lulu, he has grown it into a place where guests can stay close to nature and experience wildlife in a way that feels personal and unfiltered
At the heart of Senyati is its floodlit waterhole. There are no fences between the animals and the water, allowing elephants, buffalo and other wildlife to come and go throughout the day and into the night. Guests can watch from the deck or head down into the underground bunker for a completely different view.
Over the years, Senyati has grown to offer campsites, self-catering chalets and the Chobe Glamper, but the reason for being here has stayed the same.
To give people a place where the wildlife comes to them.
More than a place to stay
Today, Louw and Lulu are still at the heart of Senyati. What they have created is not just a place to sleep, but a camp shaped around the wildlife that passes through it and the people who come to experience it.
Some days are spent exploring Chobe National Park or the Chobe River. Others are spent right here, watching elephants gather at the waterhole, enjoying a drink on the deck or seeing what arrives after dark.
At Senyati, the bush is not something you have to go looking for. It is part of where you stay.
